output:
**An open letter to my friends, neighbours, Little Acorns families, and everyone who has been checking in**

First, I’m safe. I’m staying with my sister in Rondebosch, and Marmalade is safe too. Everyone got out of Lindale Court. I know some of you are only hearing about the fire now, or have seen messages being forwarded without much information, so I wanted to put everything in one place.

My phone hasn’t stopped since Saturday night. Please know that I am reading your messages, even when I don’t manage to answer. I’m very tired, and telling the story over and over is more than I can do at the moment. This letter is my way of answering some of your questions and saying thank you. You’re welcome to forward it.

**What happened**

At about 11:40pm on Saturday, 7 November, a fire started in a ground-floor flat at Lindale Court on Station Road in Observatory. My flat, number 12, is on the second floor. There are 14 flats in the block, and everyone managed to get out. Two people were treated for smoke inhalation at Groote Schuur and have since been sent home.

The fire department has said it was probably an electrical fault, but the investigation is still happening. I don’t want to speculate beyond that.

My neighbour, Uncle Faizel, banged on every door on our floor in his vest and slippers. That’s how I woke up. I grabbed my phone and Marmalade, and nothing else. Marmalade then hid under a car for two hours, which was a very long two hours.

There is smoke and water damage throughout my flat, and the lounge ceiling came down. My landlord has said nobody can move back in for at least six weeks. I’m still working out what can be saved and what happens next, but I’ve lost the use of my home and a lot of what was in it.

That’s the short version. I’m not ready to share a more detailed account, and I’d be grateful if people could give me a little space around that.

**Thank you**

People have been incredibly kind. One of my children’s moms left a bag of clothes at my sister’s gate at 7am on Sunday, without even knocking. I keep thinking about that. Someone woke up that morning, thought about what I might need, and quietly brought it over.

There have been so many messages, offers and small acts of care. I’ve cried reading more of them than I can count. If I haven’t replied to yours, it isn’t because it didn’t matter.

And Uncle Faizel: thank you. I don’t have enough words yet for what you did.

I keep reminding myself that furniture can be replaced. Marmalade can’t. I’m so grateful we’re both here.

**What would help right now**

I hate asking for help. I feel awkward even writing this part, and I’ve felt very strange about having a fundraiser in my name. Zinhle’s response was basically, “Shut up and accept it,” so I’m trying to listen to her.

The things I actually need at the moment are:

- **Help towards a deposit for a new place.** This is the biggest practical worry right now.
- **School shoes in size 6 and work clothes in size 34.** These are specific gaps, rather than a general request for clothing.
- **A working laptop.** If anyone has an older one they no longer use, it would make a huge difference. All my lesson planning was on mine.

Please don’t feel you need to buy anything new. And please don’t feel that you have to give anything at all. I know everyone has their own expenses and worries.

**What I don’t need**

I have enough general clothing now, thanks to everyone who has already helped. I’ll pass any extras on to people from the other flats who can use them.

I also don’t need food at the moment. My sister’s freezer is full. We’re very well looked after on that front, so please save yourselves the cooking and the trip.

I’m being specific because I don’t want anyone spending money or making a journey for something we already have.

**The fundraiser — and an important warning**

My friend **Zinhle** has set up a BackaBuddy fundraiser for me:

**backabuddy.example/thandi-lindale-court**

The target is **R25 000**, and as of this morning it had reached **R11 400**. That is an enormous amount of help. Thank you to everyone who has donated or shared it.

**This is the only fundraiser authorised by me.**

There is also a page circulating called **“Thandi Fire Relief”**, as well as a WhatsApp message asking people to EFT money into a **Capitec account**. **Those are not mine and are not connected to our fundraiser.** I have reported them.

Please don’t donate through those messages or forward them on. If you’ve already shared one, please send a correction to the same people. If you’d like to share the real fundraiser, please use Zinhle’s BackaBuddy link above.

**For the Little Acorns families**

To the parents at Little Acorns Pre-Primary in Mowbray: the concert on **27 November is still happening**. The Ladybirds will have crowns, I promise.

The 22 crowns I’d taken home to laminate, along with the children’s handprint banner, were lost in the fire. That has been a particularly sore little part of all this. But we’ll make a plan.

I’ll be back at school on Wednesday. Please don’t make a big thing of it in front of the children. I appreciate how much you care; I’d just like to get back to being their teacher without having to talk through the fire at the classroom door.

Lastly, please bear with me. I’ll reply to comments slowly, and I may not get to all my DMs. Please don’t be offended or feel you need to send another message to make sure I saw the first one.

Thank you for looking after me, for helping the other families in our block, and for giving me room to catch my breath.

With love,  
**Thandi**
